summary.one_liner: A Haskell implementation of a small Scheme interpreter, paired with a written tutorial on building one, by Adam Wespiser.
summary.what_it_does: The repository contains a reference Scheme interpreter written in Haskell, which can be run as an interactive REPL or by executing a Scheme source file. It includes a test suite (test-hs/Spec.hs) run via stack test. The tutorial text is generated into HTML and MediaWiki (Wikipedia-style) files from the docs build target. Helper scripts wrap common tasks for both the stack and cabal build tools. The README describes the project as a Write You a Scheme tutorial companion rather than a full-featured Scheme.
use_cases: learn how to write an interpreter in Haskell
follow a tutorial on building a programming language
how_to_run: ./run -s test/let.scheme to run a Scheme file
stack exec scheme to run the reference implementation
stack test to run the test suite
notable: Tutorial text is built into HTML and MediaWiki files from the same source
Works with either stack or cabal via shortcut scripts
Includes an interactive shell and file runner
